gold_with_text_not_included.reason: Task fMRI (I1) with instructed reappraisal to increase or decrease negative emotion versus look (I2), using IAPS aversive images (I3), in 23 healthy women (I4). Reports within-group increase > look and decrease > look contrasts (I5) as whole-brain voxelwise maps in MNI space (I6). Original empirical data (E1 not met), whole-brain rather than ROI-only (E2), task activation rather than connectivity (E3), within-group effects reported (E4 not met), regulation instructed rather than empathy (E5 not met). No analyses were listed in the batch, so no analysis decisions are given.

The text file holds only a stub: one table caption and an analysis definition, with no Methods (task, stimuli, participants, acquisition) or Results. The batch flags it as likely incomplete, and the criteria cannot be judged from it. Returned to retrieval.

Event-related fMRI reappraisal study (view/increase/decrease) of IAPS threat pictures in 24 healthy women (I1-I5 met). However, every reported analysis uses ROI-restricted (small-volume) correction within atlas-defined amygdala, ACC, DLPFC and OFC masks; no whole-brain voxelwise result is reported (E2 met, I6 not demonstrated, so not_met).

The text file holds only an abstract-level record: no sample details, no analysis methods, no inference settings, no tables or coordinates. Methods and Results are missing, so I4-I6 and E2-E4 cannot be judged; returned to retrieval rather than excluded.

Task fMRI (I1) of reappraisal of aversive IAPS pictures (I2, I3) in 30 healthy adults (I4). Reports whole-brain voxel-wise maps (FDR, MNI) built on the within-task ReappNeg - LookNeg contrast (I5, I6), related to reappraisal success, plus mediation maps. Not connectivity (E3), not between-group (E4). Note: the reported maps are across-subject correlation/mediation maps rather than group-mean contrast maps; handled at selection.

Block-design fMRI emotion regulation task in healthy male and female students: participants reduced their negative or positive emotion versus simply viewing IAPS pictures (I1-I4 met; instructed cognitive control of emotion qualifies for I2). Regulate vs view contrasts are reported (I5). A second-level whole-brain ANOVA with MNI coordinates is reported (I6 met, E2 not met). Within-sex post hoc paired t-tests (regulate > view per sex) exist, so E4 is not met.

Text file is only a minimal stub (title, group names, a one-line task description); it has no Methods detail or Results, and no tables. Criteria I2-I6 cannot be judged. Returned to retrieval as incomplete.

The text file is a sparse extraction record lacking the Methods: no acquisition, task, instructed regulation strategy, stimulus modality, participant details or whole-brain inference settings are described. Only contrast names (e.g. Regulation > Perception, I5) and table captions are present, so I1-I4 and I6 cannot be assessed. Returned for retrieval rather than excluded.

Healthy adults (I4) doing an IAPS picture reappraisal task in fMRI (I1-I3, I5). The methods mention a whole-brain group Reappraise > Negative t-test, but the text reports no whole-brain peak coordinates, tables or results for it. The only reported result is an anatomical amygdala ROI analysis. Group-level whole-brain peak coordinates in standard space were not demonstrated (I6 not met). E2 is unclear because a whole-brain analysis is described but its results are not reported.

Task fMRI reappraisal (Reduce vs Maintain) of negative IAPS images with whole-brain Talairach results (I1-I3, I5, I6 met). I4 not met: the high-anxiety group is a clinical population (12 of 13 met full anxiety-disorder criteria), and the only within-group regulation contrast pools it with the normal-anxiety group. No separate control-group result is reported; the other results are group-by-task interactions. The pooled Reduce > Maintain map is a within-sample effect, so E4 is not met.

Event-related fMRI emotion regulation study in 30 healthy adults (I1, I4) with instructed reappraisal to decrease emotional response to IAPS pictures (I2, I3), compared with view and distraction (I5). Whole-brain second-level random-effects analyses with FDR correction in MNI space, with activation tables (Tables 2-4) alongside PPI (I6; E2, E3 not met). Single group, so no between-group-only issue (E4). Note: the only extracted analyses are amygdala PPI maps, which are ineligible under selection.

Task fMRI (I1) in which participants were instructed to regulate by taking the position of a detached observer (I2) while viewing IAPS pictures (I3). MDD patients and healthy controls, with control-group results reported separately (I4). Reports within-group negative > neutral contrasts (I5) as whole-brain FWE-corrected maps in MNI space (I6). PPI/ROI analyses are additional, not the only results (E2, E3 not met); within-group effects exist (E4 not met).

Task fMRI reappraisal study (I1, I2) with negative pictures (I3) and whole-brain MNI results (I5, I6). However, the sample is BPD patients plus healthy controls, and the within-group effects (negative > neutral, decrease > maintain, increase > maintain) are reported for the complete pooled group; control-group results are only shown as HC vs BPD differences, never separately (I4 not met).

Task fMRI in 19 healthy women viewing emotional pictures under natural viewing (NAT), cognitive reappraisal (REAP, down-regulation by viewing scenes as fake) and expressive suppression (I1-I4). Reports whole-brain within-group SPM2 contrasts in MNI space, including REAP vs ESUP and instruction x content interactions (I5, I6). No exclusion applies.

Task fMRI (I1) in healthy women (I4) viewing food images (I3) with whole-brain MNI results (I6). However, the regulated response is appetitive desire to eat (craving), not an emotional response: participants downregulated their desire for tasty food by thinking of long-term consequences versus admitting the desire. This is appetite/craving regulation rather than emotion regulation (I2 not met), and the contrasts (REGULATE vs ADMIT, tasty vs non-tasty food) are not emotion-regulation or emotional-viewing contrasts (I5 not met).

Cognitive reappraisal task (Up/Down/Maintain) with BPD, trauma-exposed non-PTSD and healthy control groups. The only results reported are between-group differences in Up vs Maintain and Down vs Maintain (E4 met). No within-group effect is reported for any group, including controls (I5 not met). The text does not show that the stimuli were visual (I3 not demonstrated) or that the analysis was whole-brain (I6 not demonstrated).

Task fMRI in healthy women (I1, I4) regulating responses to violent victim-offender pictures via reappraisal-based disengage/engage instructions (I2, I3, I5; E5 not met since regulation was instructed). However every reported analysis is restricted to atlas ROIs with ROI-scoped inference; no whole-brain voxelwise map with coordinates is reported (I6 not met, E2 met).

Task-based fMRI (I1) of cognitive reappraisal to decrease negative affect (I2) while viewing IAPS and similar pictures (I3), in a healthy sample aged 10-22 (I4). It reports a within-subject look negative > look neutral contrast (I5), analysed whole-brain with AlphaSim correction in Talairach space (I6). The paper is empirical, the analysis is whole-brain task activation within a single group, and it is not an empathy study, so E1-E5 are not met.

Task fMRI of reappraisal and distraction vs view of IAPS images in remitted MDD and healthy controls (I1-I5 met). All reported results are ROI analyses (amygdala, OFC, dmPFC atlas ROIs, FWE-corrected within ROI) comparing groups; no whole-brain voxelwise map with peak coordinates is reported (E2 met, I6 not met), and only between-group contrasts are reported (E4 met).

Task fMRI reappraisal of negative/neutral IAPS pictures in 58 healthy adults (I1-I5 met), but every reported analysis is restricted to atlas ROIs (DLPFC, lateral OFC, amygdala) with ROI-level FWE correction; no whole-brain voxelwise map is reported (I6 not met, E2 met).

Cognitive reappraisal task with IAPS pictures in cocaine users and controls (I1-I4 met). The only reported analysis is a PPI connectivity comparison between cocaine users with vs without personality disorders during Maintain>Observe; no whole-brain task activation map or within-group effect is reported (E3, E4 met; I5, I6 not demonstrated).

Task fMRI reappraisal study (Decrease vs Look on negative images) in 157 healthy community volunteers (I1-I5 met). The only reported analysis is an anatomically defined dACC ROI entered into a mediation model with IL-6 and atherosclerosis; no whole-brain voxelwise map with peak coordinates is reported (I6 not met, E2 met).

Task fMRI (I1) with instructed cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation) vs React (I2). Two of three tasks use visual stimuli (angry/contemptuous face photos, videotaped criticism), meeting I3; the Beliefs task uses written sentences. SAD patients plus healthy controls whose Reappraise > React effects are reported separately (I4, E4 not met). Within-task reappraisal contrasts (I5) from whole-brain AlphaSim-corrected voxelwise maps in Talairach space (I6, E2 not met). Not connectivity-only (E3), not an empathy study (E5), empirical (E1). The only extracted analysis is a between-group contrast, so it may yield no eligible analysis, but study screening criteria are all satisfied.

Task fMRI (I1) of younger and older adults (I4) reappraising or selectively attending to emotional film clips (I2, I3) with within-group regulation vs passive viewing contrasts (I5). However, all voxelwise analyses were restricted to an explicit amygdala-PFC mask with ROI-scope AlphaSim correction; no whole-brain analysis is reported (E2 met, I6 not met).

Task fMRI (I1) where participants regulated responses to aversive IAPS-type photographs by distancing (far) vs reacting (close) (I2, I3), in 56 healthy 10-23-year-olds (I4). Reports within-task regulation/negative > reactivity/negative and negative > neutral contrasts (I5). Most analyses are amygdala ROI or PPI, but the passive re-presentation regulation > reactivity contrast is recorded as a whole-brain mixed-effects model in MNI space (I6 met; E2, E3 not met). Within-subject design with age as a covariate, not only between-group (E4 not met). Not empathy (E5 not met).

Task fMRI reappraisal (distancing) study with IAPS social images in avoidant personality disorder vs healthy participants (I1-I3 met). Every reported analysis is a patient-versus-control group difference (Reappraise Cue>Look Cue and Look Negative>Look Neutral, avoidant vs healthy), including the only whole-brain analysis; no within-group task effect is reported for any group, so E4 is met, and the healthy control group's results are not reported separately (I4 not met).

Task fMRI (I1) with instructed acceptance and reappraisal (I2) of sad IAPS/photographic images (I3); control group reported separately (I4); within-group accept > view and reappraise > accept contrasts (I5). However, the group analyses were restricted to an a priori search mask covering only the frontal lobes and bilateral amygdala, i.e. partial brain coverage, with no accompanying whole-brain analysis (E2 met; I6 not demonstrated, so not_met), despite the record labelling the scope as whole-brain.

Task fMRI (I1) in 15 expert meditators (I4) with instructed positive Reappraisal and Compassion regulation conditions plus Watch conditions (I2) while viewing film clips of people in distress (I3). Reports within-group whole-brain contrasts such as Compassion vs Watch-Negative (I5), cluster-corrected across a whole-brain grey-matter mask with MNI coordinates (I6). Original empirical data (E1 not met); not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity-only (E3), not between-group-only (E4). Participants were instructed to regulate their own affect, so E5 does not apply. No extracted analyses were supplied for this study.

Healthy adults reappraised IAPS negative images and were re-exposed one week later (I1-I5 met). Every reported analysis is recorded with ROI spatial scope and restricted to one right-amygdala cluster. The inference settings list a whole-brain FWE scope but name the amygdala as the correction region. No group-level whole-brain voxelwise map with peak coordinates was demonstrated, so I6 is not met. E2 is unclear because of this conflict.

Task fMRI (I1) with instructed cognitive self-distancing (I2) toward IAPS aversive pictures (I3) in healthy women (I4), with a Distance > Attend contrast (I5). However, the only reported analysis is a generalized PPI connectivity result between a vlPFC seed and a midbrain-masked VTA ROI; no whole-brain task-activation peak coordinates are reported in the text, so I6 was not demonstrated. The vlPFC seed was defined from a Distance > Attend activation contrast, but its coordinates are not given, so E3 is left unclear.

Whole-brain fMRI reappraisal vs maintain task with negative IAPS images (I1-I3, I5, I6 met) in 18 panic disorder patients and 18 healthy controls. I4 requires that a clinical study report the control group's results separately; the only within-task contrasts (Reappraisal > Maintain, Maintain > Reappraisal) are main effects pooled across patients and controls, and the remaining analyses are patient-vs-control group differences, interactions or connectivity. Controls' results are never reported separately, so I4 is not demonstrated.

Task fMRI in 108 healthy adults (I1, I4). Participants down-regulated by self-focused reappraisal (distancing) while viewing Emotional Picture Set pictures (I2, I3). A whole-brain RegulateNeg > WatchNeg contrast in MNI space is reported (I5, I6). Alongside the amygdala ROI and PPI analyses there is a within-group whole-brain activation map, so E2-E4 are not met. No analyses were extracted for this study.

Task fMRI study of positive and minimizing reappraisal of IAPS images in healthy adults (I1-I5 met). The only reported result is a PPI connectivity effect between vmPFC and left amygdala, small-volume corrected; no group-level whole-brain task activation map with coordinates is reported (I6 not demonstrated; E2 and E3 met).
